Subject: Shed project

DRAFT — Shed redo, part two: the part where I explain why we did not simply put a nice rug over everything and call it a day.

I spent the last two Saturdays getting a shed’s electrical sorted out. The “before” list was so long it needed its own union card. Three orange extension cords daisy-chained out a basement window, across the yard and under the deck. One splice wrapped in duct tape. A 30-amp breaker feeding 14-gauge wire. An outlet connected with speaker wire. And the “GFCI”? A regular outlet wearing a GFCI sticker, which is a bold career change but not an actual safety feature.

The ceiling fan box was held up by one drywall screw. There was a mouse nest in a junction box, and the mice seemed perfectly content with their accommodations. Inside the panel door, somebody had helpfully written “SHED — DON’T TOUCH — RON.” I opened the panel and the wife standing there asked, “Who’s Ron?” Fair question. At that point, I was wondering if Ron was still in there.

We fixed it properly: trenched for buried cable, installed the right breaker and wiring, and put in real boxes, outlets and a fan brace. The mice were left to pursue other real estate. I was paid in two pizzas and a case of Yuengling, which is a respectable package unless the pizza was also expected to pass inspection.

This isn’t a story about some cartoon villain. The guy wasn’t evil; he was cheap and a little proud. That’s most of these situations. Somebody figures they can save a few bucks, borrows a video’s confidence, and turns a shed into a collection of “that’ll probably be fine.” I get the temptation. I also get called when “probably” starts smelling like burning.

Electrical mistakes don’t always give you a warning, and a sticker, a YouTube tutorial, or a buddy who’s handy isn’t a substitute for the right work. Bad wiring can shock somebody or start a fire that takes the whole house with it. If you need electrical work, call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy with a YouTube video. Please.

No names, no address, and no shame parade—just a reminder that the funny-looking shortcuts can be dangerous. I’ll add the pictures once I’ve picked the ones that don’t make the shed look like it needs its own lawyer.
